newsitem.title: UK: Tomkins puzzled by level of investor demand.
newsitem.headline: Tomkins puzzled by level of investor demand.

text.p: Tomkins Plc, the food to engineering combine, said on Monday it was puzzled by the level of investor demand for its shares and blamed the current anti-conglomerate sentiment in the UK market.

Greg Hutchings, executive chairman of the group which earlier announced a bumper 34 percent rise in half-year pre-tax profits to 168.8 million stg earlier, told a press briefing: "In general 95 percent of analysts are saying to their clients buy our shares. So it must be the investors (who are not listening)." He concluded the company was a victim of the fact conglomerates were out of fashion.

Shares in the company had initially risen after the results which were better than expected. But the chairman later said in an interview with Reuters that Tomkins was unlikely to launch a buyback and favoured acquisitions instead, leading shares to fall back, say market makers.
Shares are currently down three and a half pence at 274 in a positive market after seeing a strong run-up last week on buyback hopes and analysts' buy recommendations.
Tomkins bosses tried to distinguish themselves from the conglomerates sector, pointing out that they had acheived earnings per share growth for 12 years running.
The company also said its return on capital employed was 18.6 percent, well ahead of the sector average.

Turning to the performance of Gates, the industrial and auto components group bought last summer for $1.1 billion, the group said it planned a programme of capital expenditure. It sees savings of at least $12 million per annum from efficiency improvements to the information systems. Tomkins said most of the benefits from this acquisition still lay ahead.
